scope: Finite normalizer Hodge-model comparison and order-3/order-32 cotangent bounds; global RR and exact identification remain open.

external_sources.title: Yuan: Modular Heights of Quaternionic Shimura Curves
external_sources.role: Maximal Hodge system, order-3 CM height with no common ramification, and equality of the coarse orbifold line away from 2. Normalizer quotient and dyadic comparison are derived in the report.

external_sources.title: Yuan and Zhang: On the averaged Colmez conjecture
external_sources.role: Averaged CM identities and structural Hodge pullback/dualizing statements; relative Shimura-point heights are divided by 8.

external_sources.title: Zhao: Heights of Special Points on Quaternionic Shimura Varieties
external_sources.role: Order-32 CM height with common dyadic ramification. D104 normalization reconciliation retained; the inconsistent final proof display of Theorem 7.5 is not used. This theorem is not applied to E3.

external_sources.title: Liu and Lorenzini: Models of curves and finite covers
external_sources.role: Stable extension of the generic small-level map; finite special-fibre extension is not assumed for the derivative inequality. Inherited D104 applicability.

external_sources.title: Kurihara: On some examples of equations defining Shimura curves and the Mumford uniformization
external_sources.role: Inherited D99/D119 normal quotient and inverted-edge smooth-disk model. D143 computes the arithmetic Hodge multidegrees and marked-tail correction on that certified model.

external_sources.title: Stacks Project: A formula for the different
external_sources.role: Generic-component monogenic derivative formula used by the diagnostic; the independent graph reconstruction instead uses multidegrees and the trivial-stabilizer normalization.
